issues.detail: The skill is tied to Blender's Python API and specific version assumptions (5.0+ layered actions, with differing 4.x behaviour), and the video tracking section requires the Movie Clip Editor UI context so it cannot run in the headless `--background` mode the compatibility note recommends.

scenarios.name: retarget-mixamo-to-rigify-5x
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely (target:source mapping, per-frame frame_set, new action with animation_data creation, rotation_quaternion keyframes, location on the root only, no fcurves access), while A uses matrix-based world-space retargeting with inverted mapping direction (source:target), keys rotation_euler as a fallback, and keys extra IK_FK props, deviating from the rubric's simple copy approach and mapping direction.

scenarios.name: decimate-mocap-fcurves-blender5
scenarios.rationale: Both reach F-curves via layers→strips→channelbag(slot).fcurves with animation_data.action_slot, preserve first/last keys, call fcurve.update(), and note action.fcurves is gone in 5.x; B adds a strip.type check, RDP-based error-aware thinning and fuller usage notes, but A states more explicitly that action.fcurves fails and is simpler, while B's removal with fast=True followed by update() is also fine.

scenarios.name: track-and-solve-camera-from-footage
scenarios.rationale: Response A satisfies the rubric: it loads the clip, sets tracking and camera settings, calls detect_features, track_markers, clean_tracks and solve_camera, compares average_error to 0.5 px, and states that bpy.ops.clip.* needs a Movie Clip Editor context and fails under --background; Response B covers the same pipeline but tells the user to run with -b and only hedges that the context override 'should work', which contradicts the required statement.
